sections.heading: 8. Static prop self-shadowing (buildings read flat / cardboard)

blocks.html: User report (mc2_10 night): a building's light-facing parts are FULLY lit and its away-facing parts dark, but nothing accounts for occlusion by the building's own geometry — a wall behind a taller wing, a recessed courtyard, an inset doorway or the underside of an overhang all render full-bright.

NEW 2026-07-25. Deterministic 3840x2160 engine captures, exe 16c2244a. Day = clean quantitative; night = categorical (see caveat).

blocks.html: NO CODE CHANGE WAS NEEDED — and none was made. Both mechanisms were already shipped and simply switched off. Root cause is three stacked things: (1) static_prop.frag writes the a=0.25 "no self shadow" GBuffer class and shadow_screen.frag deliberately skips the dynamic cascade for it ("CPU never self-shadowed buildings"); (2) the baked base light is a per-LEAF constant (GetARGBHighlight(), one scalar per TG_Shape), so it adds no intra-surface variation, and calc_light has no occlusion term at all; (3) what is left is a pure per-face max(N·L,0) — precisely "fully lit or dark, nothing between". Props already cast into the CSM cascades, so no caster-set widening was required and the alpha-card foliage exclusion was never touched.

Why BOTH gates. MC2_PROP_SHADOW_RECEIVE opts props back into the dynamic cascade — that gives coarse wing-on-wing shadow, but the cascades are map-sized and cannot resolve a doorway reveal. MC2_SSAO adds the fine contact term (recesses, inside corners, undersides) using depth + GBuffer normals props already write. Measured on mc2_01 day: RECEIVE alone changes 0.25-0.73% of pixels and 100% of them get DARKER, zero brighter (a pure occlusion term can only darken — animation or a lighting bug could not be one-sided); adding SSAO multiplies coverage 20-60x (to 1.5-14.7%) while staying ~99% darker.

RESIDUAL — this is why neither gate should default ON yet. Alpha-test lattice props self-shadow as solid slabs: the shadow depth pass has no alpha discard, so a chain-link fence writes a solid depth slab into the cascades and then, with RECEIVE ON, samples that slab and darkens uniformly across the whole lattice (image below — it is the single densest diff region on the day poses). Foliage is protected from this by setRecipeNoShadow; fences and railings are not foliage and are not excluded. The clean fix needs a distinct GBuffer1.a class for alpha-test props so they can be excluded from receive — that edits the render-contract mask encoding shared with shadow_screen.frag, too wide to land unverified, so it is logged as follow-up PROP-ALPHA-SHADOW-CLASS-1 rather than guessed at here. The cheap alternative (marking alpha-test recipes noShadow) is wrong — it would also stop fences casting onto terrain.

⚠ REVIEW-LANES-LOG-2 CORRECTION — prop self-shadow CANNOT fix the building-face complaint, and MC2_SSAO is broken rather than merely off. Three corrections to this section. (1) A face turned away from the sun already has ndl = 0; a shadow term multiplying zero changes nothing, so MC2_PROP_SHADOW_RECEIVE is architecturally incapable of addressing it — measured, it moves 0.005-0.183% of pixels and only on props like aircraft. (2) The follow-up premise that base_light was the culprit is falsified: a gate built on it was byte-identical at strength 1.0, which multiplies the seed by zero — base_light is effectively ZERO on these props, day and night. The term that actually lights them is ambientTerm, the orientation-free per-actor object-light ambient; that is the real cure site. (3) MC2_SSAO is latent-broken, not off: the AO buffer is white (mean 254.99/255) because aoRadius_ is 3.0 world units against a 42.67 wu map cell — 2% of one cell — and there is no blur pass at all, only a 4-tap box over ±0.5 of a half-res texel, which cannot denoise a 16-sample stochastic kernel. Raising the radius alone therefore trades no-occlusion for visible dither. The 20-60× coverage figure quoted above should not be relied on. (SHADOW-DECISIONS-1, SSAO-RETUNE-1, PROP-BASE-LIGHT-DIR-1.)

blocks.html: Root cause. The min-screen-size clamp added by f412423e was max(1.0, kLbMinNdc / sil) with no upper bound. sil falls off as 1/distance, so k grew without limit and pinned every fixture to a constant hard-edged bright block at every camera distance. Holding a constant screen size was the clamp's literal intent — correct at playable RTS range, which is what made the lights visible at grazing angles — but past that range several hundred regularly-spaced fixtures simply never shrink. Regular spacing + constant size = the dashes. A secondary error compounded it ~1.5x: kLbRefRadius was the authored top-cap radius (0.8), but the rigid billboard maps local Z (the 2.85-unit post axis) onto toCam, so the post foreshortens and the viewer actually sees the local XY cross-section (runwaylight.ase extents 2.015 x 2.326, radius ~1.2). The clamp was sizing against a feature that is never on screen.

Fix. clamp(kLbMinNdc/sil, 1.0, kLbMaxScale) with kLbMaxScale = 2.5 and the corrected reference radius — the legitimate win survives (fixtures still rasterise at playable range) but they resume normal 1/distance shrink and go sub-pixel at overview on their own. Plus the gate is now default-OFF so stock is what ships.

Measured (changed px, |d|>8, BEFORE vs opt-in): overview 549 px in a 136 x 13 horizontal band, 95% of them darker, max delta 240 — that band is the streak. Oblique airbase 9019 px; near-top-down 1817 px. Close ground-level: 0 px, max delta 0 — byte-identical, proving the cap is inactive at close range and gameplay-zoom appearance is untouched.

PopulateRecipeCementWords bakes a cement word for a TRANSITION tile only when a corner terrainType resolves to a SOLID cement layer and a corner mask derives. Provenance limit, stated plainly. Read verdicts precisely. APPROVED BY USER means the user saw it and said yes — do not regress it. REJECTED BY USER means the user saw it and said no — do not revive it or present it as a candidate. lanes.name: SHADOW-SUNCLAMP-1
lanes.sent: Act on DROPPED-ITEMS-1's unclamped-sun finding and fix the reported world-scale shadowed-half / unshadowed-half split on mc2_10.
lanes.found: The handed-over root cause was refuted by its own A/B. Three wide mc2_10 night poses plus a liveness arm came back byte-identical gate ON vs OFF (sunclamp_center_wide hashes ea1688351a3d60a7 both ways) — because the NdotL guard only exists in sampleDynamicShadow, on the mech path, and terrain/grass/decals early-out before ever reading lightDir. The lane then located the real mechanism on the terrain path: shadow.hglsl resets normal=(0,0,1) under MC2_SHADOW_STATIC_BANDFIX_V2 (default ON) before the guard, so on mc2_10 (LightDirPitch 180) NdotL ≈ 0 < 0.05 and terrain sun shadows are suppressed globally while props/mechs keep theirs. Handed to TERRAIN-SHADOW-GUARD-1, which confirmed it.

lanes.name: TERRAIN-SHADOW-GUARD-1
lanes.sent: Land and capture-confirm the terrain-path fix for the NdotL-guard-on-raw-sun mechanism SHADOW-SUNCLAMP-1 located but could not land.
lanes.found: Confirmed by capture, not by argument. With the gate OFF, MC2_LIGHTING_DEBUG_VIEW=shadow renders the terrain shadow-factor buffer as featureless saturated white — 70.0% of the frame above 250/255 on sunclamp_center_wide, the literal return 1.0 early-out firing for every terrain pixel. With the gate ON that falls to 2.9% and relief-following terrain shadow structure appears (69.4%→28.1% on sunclamp_relief_ne). The fix landed broader than briefed — inside calcShadow/calcDynamicShadow, so it also covers decal, grass and terrain-overlay frags. Purely subtractive: 0.00% of pixels brightened in any pose. lanes.name: PERF-HARNESS-TRUTH-1
lanes.sent: Fix the performance harness so GPU/fragment-bound cost is visible, and deliver the light-grid frame-time table LIGHT-CLUSTER-PERF-1 owed.
lanes.found: The inherited diagnosis was false on both counts — no window consumer reads MC2_SMOKE_MODE, and the 10 ms throttle is OS show-state-driven, not harness-driven; with a visible window the two arms still measured within 0.2%. The real cause: the harness reported CPU-side DrawScreen zone duration, which cannot show GPU fragment cost because GL submission is async — raising the per-fragment loop 4× genuinely did not move CPU time. Separately MC2_LOG was never set, so all nine .game.log files were zero bytes: the runs were not merely wrong, they were unverifiable. Once fixed (true frame-interval timing + visible window + receipt verification), the light grid lands at or slightly below the cap=64 baseline (night_busy p50 6.679→6.481 ms, −3.0%) and MC2_LIGHT_REALISM costs nothing measurable.

lanes.name: PAVED-OVERLAY-CLASS-1
lanes.sent: Close the classification gap ROAD-OVERLAY-LIGHT-1 found — roads/runways on non-cement slots never reaching the cement classify chain.

But the mean tone offset did not uniformly converge: it closes 50-94% where pavement was darker than cement, and widens by up to 483% where pavement was already brighter — because once both are flat-lit the residue is pure albedo, which no lighting-side lever can reach. (This was previously cited as “the same wall PROP-LIGHT-CLASS-4 hit on trucks”; that cross-reference is RETRACTED — the truck finding was a region-mean artifact and is withdrawn. The pavement-albedo residue here is a separate, independently measured result and stands on its own.) lanes.name: CONE-SPILL-GRADE-1
lanes.sent: Adversarially grade two lanes (CONE-SPILL-COUPLING-1, EDGE-LIGHT-EMISSION-1) that shipped code and died without ever being reviewed.
lanes.found: c1f98b45 is REGRESSIVE and is now default-OFF. It deletes 7 of the 9 night ground light pools on mc2_10 (POOLS_KEPT 9/9 → 2/9) in exchange for moving the 2 survivors by 7 world units and removing a 200.0f clamp that fires 0/9 times. Cause: stock fixtures are authored near-horizontal (14.9 units of drop over a 167.8-unit beam) so the ray/terrain intersection almost never lands on ground, and the miss-rejection wrongly counts buildings (absent from the heightfield) and border terrain as misses. It was riding an unregistered, undocumented, default-ON gate (MC2_LIGHT_CONE_NODES) with no gate of its own. EDGE-LIGHT-EMISSION-1 by contrast is a real fix, but saturating — see its row.

lanes.name: NIGHT-TAGS-GREEN-1
lanes.sent: Implement a scoped Hot-Green-only mode for MC2_STATIC_PROP_NIGHT_TAGS, on the premise that Hot Green tags are exclusive to runway/beacon fixtures.
lanes.found: The premise is false, and the lane refused to build on it. Of 738 meshes carrying Hot Green (0xff00ff00) in data/tgl/*.ase, only 8 are beacon/runway fixtures — the other 730 are buildings (barracks, palaces, city blocks, HPG, turrets). The shader says so itself at lighting.hglsl:118: Hot Green — Building Base Lights. Cross-checked in data: of 274 .ini files declaring HotGreenRGB, only 4 use it as a beacon emission colour; 270 use it as a building base glow. A green-only mode would relight ~270 building types to fix ~8 fixture types — a larger blast radius than the all-branch gate it was meant to narrow, aimed straight at the user's separate over-lit-buildings complaint.

lanes.name: CAPTURE-DETERMINISM-1
lanes.sent: Characterise and where possible fix the run-to-run nondeterminism in mc2_10 captures that had been invalidating pixel-A/B evidence across many lanes.
lanes.found: Reproduced the problem worse than briefed: up to 27.3% of pixels differing across three launches with byte-identical env. Found and fixed one real cause — code/mechcmd2.cpp:2245 computed frameLength from the real measured framerate even under MC2_SMOKE_FIXED_TIMESTEP, so movers integrated a different dt each launch; pinning it dropped lance_close noise 20.4%→0.269%. Raising settle frames 30→150 cut saved_204937 23.4%→15.5% but never reaches zero. A third source remains open and unpinned (12.4-15.5%): mc2_10 captures are still not reproducible. Sim/render frame skew and streaming/LOD were explicitly refuted as causes.

lanes.name: LIGHT-REALISM-FLIP-1
lanes.sent: Decide whether MC2_LIGHT_REALISM should flip default-ON, by grading variant B against the user's four night-lighting complaints.
lanes.found: Three of the four complaints (feathered cones, spill continuity, LIGHT SOURCE-like beacons) are convincingly solved. The fourth is measurably worsened. MC2_LIGHT_REALISM_POOL_SPILL=2.2 scales farDistance for every pool light uniformly, including near-camera mover lights, and hot-pixel area explodes at lance_close from 0.360% to 8.250% — 23×; at the user's own grading poses 11× and 6.3×. The proposed cure (spare mover lights) was handed to POOL-SPILL-STATIC-1, which proved it inert. Half this lane's matrix never ran: the A: volume hit 0 bytes free and 12 of 14 PNGs in one arm were written zero-byte.

lanes.name: POOL-SPILL-STATIC-1
lanes.sent: Implement LIGHT-REALISM-FLIP-1's prescribed cure — apply pool spill to static lights only, sparing mover lights — and verify it removes the blowout.
lanes.found: Implemented, proven INERT, and reverted. MC2_LIGHT_POOL_DUMP=1 receipts at the user's exact complaint poses show the light rows by class are {other: 1684, bldg: 81} — zero mech, zero gv. lightIsMover() never returns true there, so the blowout is caused entirely by static/untagged lights and the mover carve-out cannot touch it. Uniform-2.2 and static-only-2.2 are numerically indistinguishable at lance_close (7.834% vs 8.288% hot area — the “fix” is fractionally worse). A dose-response sweep then found the actual lever: POOL_SPILL=1.3 keeps the cone and beacon wins whole while cutting blowout from 8.29% to 1.27%.

lanes.name: BEACON-FIXTURE-ID-1
lanes.sent: Implement an exact discriminator so stock night emission can be scoped to runway/beacon fixtures and not buildings.
lanes.found: The brief's proposed discriminator was refuted before it was built. “Saturated-primary Hot*RGB” matches 503 of 773 stock .ini files — useless — because mclib/bdactor.cpp:813-819 defaults undeclared HotGreenRGB to 0xff00ff00, so ~499 buildings inherit a saturated primary they never declared. The shipped discriminator adds an equality clause (all three equal AND saturated), narrowing to exactly 4 of 773 with zero building leakage. But the mechanism only delivers already-stock emission: get_base_light clamps at 1.0, so scales 1, 4 and 8 are byte-identical and the visible effect is +21/255 on an already-green beacon. The user's actual complaint is not closed by this.

lanes.name: FIXTURE-GLOW-1
lanes.sent: Build a bounded additive glow so runway/beacon fixtures read as lit light sources, verify it is safe at overview altitude, and decide its default.
lanes.found: Diagnosed why every prior emissive attempt was structurally doomed: static_prop.frag:436 multiplies lighting by albedo, so a dark lens texel dims any emissive seed. Fix is a separate additive term after the albedo multiply and fog. The first shipped design was falsified by its own measurement — a view-depth clip.w window is meaningless because MC2 changes altitude by scaling the projection, not moving the eye, so ground (~659) and overview (~800) eye-distances are nearly flat and the bound was unbounded at every altitude. Re-cut as an NDC-silhouette smoothstep: 2 px changed at 1× and at 4× strength against a 232 px noise floor. Also found stock data has no white fixture at all (runwaylight.ini is red) and that at 1:1 the glow only desaturates an already channel-max lens toward white — it cannot brighten it further.

lanes.name: NIGHT-AMBIENT-BALANCE-1
lanes.sent: Test whether inflated night ambient explains the truck-vs-building contrast complaint, and whether a default flip is warranted.
lanes.found: Night ambient is inflated — but by a different mechanism than everyone had been citing, and it does not explain the complaint. The widely-quoted “196/255 night ambient” figure is wrong: static_prop.vert:242's v_dbgAmbient is authored ambient plus two port-added fill terms, not the mission's raw ambient, which is stock-faithful at NightAmbient{Red,Green,Blue}=32. The real inflator is MC2_STATIC_PROP_IBL_SH — a day-sky HDRI probe applied at full strength at night with zero night scaling, multiplicative into albedo: bldg_left gains +54.2% luminance and white-clips on 2.76% of its pixels. Killing IBL does not fix the truck gap (truck/bldg_tower 0.590→0.609). This was previously written up as “independently confirming PROP-LIGHT-CLASS-4: it is albedo, not lighting” — that conclusion is RETRACTED. Both ratios came from the same region-MEAN rectangles, so they corroborated a shared measurement artifact, not a shared finding; masked re-measurement shows the truck texture is of median brightness (85.9 vs 86.2 corpus median). The IBL night-scaling finding above is unaffected. The truck cause remains in the lighting path and is OPEN.

lanes.name: IBL-NIGHT-SCALE-1
lanes.sent: Act on NIGHT-AMBIENT-BALANCE-1: night-scale the day-sky SH-IBL probe instead of killing it.
lanes.found: Landed the night-scaling curve strength *= mix(1.0, floor, nightFactor) with floor 0.25, chosen as the measured knee — it removes 95% of the clipping for a 13-18% brightness cost, against 29-46% for a blunt killswitch. On mc2_10 night, hard-clipped pixels on a building face fall 2.49% → 0.13% (19×). Found two linkage traps en route: u_nightFactor was silently zero unless an unrelated gate happened to be on, and the IBL strength is not the neutral 0.5 default it appears to be — data/visual_tuning.json overrides it per-mission to 0.55-0.6.

lanes.name: RUNWAY-LIGHT-MISSING-1
lanes.sent: Find out why runway-light props are missing campaign-wide, per the report that they are absent on mc2_10.
lanes.found: Nothing is missing. Nothing was ever being lost. Runtime receipts on mc2_01, mc2_10 and mc2_23 show placement-to-render agreement is exact on all three — nothing culled, nothing dropped. mc2_10 simply places zero runway lights (it has 32 red / 12 green / 16 blue beacons and no runway lights at all), while 365 runway lights exist across the campaign: mc2_23 has 112 at full night, mc2_01 has 56 in daylight. Five prior lanes verified fixture work on the one map that has none of the fixture in question. On maps that do have them the lights are drawn, but read as dull amber cones because emission is clamped at 1.0 then multiplied by a dark lens albedo — a brightness ceiling on present geometry, not absent geometry. The lane also caught its own first-pass table (which claimed mc2_10 had 32) as wrong, via an ordinal off-by-one, by cross-checking the engine's runtime receipt.

lanes.name: SHADOW-DECISIONS-1
lanes.sent: Grade three shadow/AO gates (MC2_SSAO, MC2_PROP_SHADOW_RECEIVE, MC2_PROP_LOD_SHADOW_CAST) against the user's building-face complaint.
lanes.found: All three recommended to stay default-OFF, each for a different reason. MC2_SSAO measures essentially zero benefit at shipped tuning — AO buffer mean 254.99/255, byte-identical at night — traced to aoRadius_ defaulting to 3.0 world units. MC2_PROP_SHADOW_RECEIVE architecturally cannot fix the complaint: a face turned away from the sun already has ndl = 0, so a shadow term multiplying it changes nothing; it moves 0.005-0.183% of pixels and only on props like aircraft, never on building faces. MC2_PROP_LOD_SHADOW_CAST landed as code but showed no demonstrable benefit across 14 day + 3 night poses — what changed were mover sprites, not tree shadows. Its identification of base_light as the culprit was itself later falsified by PROP-BASE-LIGHT-DIR-1.

lanes.name: SSAO-RETUNE-1
lanes.sent: Establish whether MC2_SSAO's zero measured benefit is a radius-tuning problem or something deeper.
lanes.found: MC2_SSAO is latent-broken, not merely off. The radius half was confirmed: aoRadius_ defaults to 3.0 world units against a 42.67 wu map cell — a mean reach of 0.87 wu, 2% of one cell — producing literally zero occlusion (0 px below 250/255). Raising it to 40 produces real structured signal at prop bases, fence lines and gantry cranes. But grading that at 1:1 overturned the “just retune it” premise by surfacing a second, independent defect: there is no blur pass at all. runSSAO is two draws, gen and apply; the only denoise is a 4-tap box spanning ±0.5 of a half-res texel, which cannot denoise a 16-sample stochastic kernel. So any radius large enough to show occlusion also shows speckled dither on flat unoccluded faces — worse than the darkening it was meant to add. A bilateral blur must land before any default-ON proposal.

lanes.name: PROP-BASE-LIGHT-DIR-1
lanes.sent: Add a directional term to static-prop base lighting to darken building faces turned away from the sun, per SHADOW-DECISIONS-1's identified root cause.
lanes.found: The inherited root cause was falsified by measurement. Built on base_light, the gate gave byte-identical output at every strength including 1.0 — which multiplies the seed by zero, and is impossible if base_light mattered. After ruling out env-drop, harness caching, wrong-shader and props-not-in-frame, the lane proved base_light is effectively ZERO on these props, day and night. The term actually lighting them is ambientTerm, the per-actor object-light ambient — orientation-free by construction, exactly the defect shape described, in a different summand. Re-pointed there it moves 2.5-6.9% of pixels, monotonic and safe. But the user's acceptance test was never demonstrated: no bookmark pose showing an actual lit-from-behind wall was ever found, and the designed foliage alpha-test exclusion does not fire (trees darken, 33,053 px on one pose).

lanes.name: GOLDEN-REBLESS-2
lanes.sent: Re-bless the visual regression goldens honestly from a deterministic, attributable build; audit pose honesty; report on a release re-cut.
lanes.found: The prior 16-entry golden registry was already entirely dead — 16/16 pointed at a deleted worktree path, so there was nothing to re-bless. Live goldens carried blessed_commit: null and no recorded env or gate state. Under a 3-run-minimum rule, 27 of 39 regions were blessed and 12 were REFUSED with measured noise floors up to 20.04% — refused rather than silently passed. Critically, v0.5.2-baseline-PROPOSED fails 32 of 39 regions (up to 96.3% pixel change), and that is real content drift from ~70 commits of night-lighting work, not noise — the same regions measure 0.0000% run-to-run. Its defining poses exist only inside a deploy install and are not version-controlled, so it is unauditable and unrecoverable. Recommendation: do not promote it.

lanes.name: DETERMINISM-RATCHET-2
lanes.sent: Make the capture-determinism ratchet actually catch nondeterministic regions, attribute the residual mc2_10 drift, and close gate-hygiene issues voiding verifications.
lanes.found: The ratchet was blind by directory depth. It globbed r1/*.png, one flat level, while captures nest two deep as crops/<bookmark>/<region>.png — so on a real 234-PNG, 3-run noisy set it saw 0 files, printed SKIP and exited 0. Fixed with rglob, empty-set-now-fails, and all-pairs --min-runs 3; it then caught all 12 regions GOLDEN-REBLESS-2 refused plus 2 more that lane had wrongly blessed, because that lane only ever compared r1-v-r2 and r1-v-r3, never r2-v-r3. Also overturned the registry-debt numbers by an order of magnitude: ENV_DROP_RISK is 620, not the 101 previously believed (830 unregistered, 726 undocumented, 5 genuine ghosts). Attributed the residual mc2_10 drift to a single target-acquisition divergence at t=34.1 s (one Centipede, id 711); mover iteration order and ASLR were explicitly refuted.

lanes.name: BUILDING-FACE-POSE-1
lanes.sent: Find and vendor a bookmark pose that actually shows the user's building-face defect, so MC2_PROP_BASE_LIGHT_DIR can be graded against it.
lanes.found: Not landed at the time this page was generated — no status document and no registered lane. It exists here because PROP-BASE-LIGHT-DIR-1 names it as the first of three things that must land before that gate's default flip is defensible. Until it does, the building-face complaint has a shipped mechanism and no pose that demonstrates it.

blocks.html: Findings that outlived their lane

These four are structural and should be treated as standing facts, each confirmed from source by the lane named:
  • Roads and runways are an Overlays channel disjoint from the cement flag. A runway laid across dirt has isCement(slot)==false, so it falls off the bottom of the classify chain, increments no drop counter, and no existing cement lever can reach it. (CEMENT-CLASSIFY-3, ROAD-OVERLAY-LIGHT-1.)
  • The class-diag legend is inverted in our notes and in the in-code comment. Shader ground truth: RED = solid cement-atlas, GREEN = transition, BLACK/dim = colormap only. Three lanes were misled before this was caught. (CEMENT-CLASSIFY-3; corrected in source by ROAD-OVERLAY-LIGHT-1.)
  • The shadow back-face guard uses the unclamped sun. The shadow matrices clamp the sun to 15° minimum altitude; the shadow_screen back-face guard dots the raw sun. mc2_10 alone has LightDirPitch 180, making the sun exactly horizontal, so the guard degenerates to purely azimuthal — a falsifiable, map-specific prediction that matched. (DROPPED-ITEMS-1; fix landed by SHADOW-SUNCLAMP-1.)
  • Foliage alpha-test shadows already shipped in June and are default-ON. The "no alpha discard" premise is true only of the depth shader. The residual defect is a now-stale justification comment excluding all LOD≥1 from casting. (DROPPED-ITEMS-1.)
Recurring process failures this session

• Unattributable builds were the single biggest tax. A shared worktree held dirty by parallel lanes meant repeated -dirty fingerprints; at least one whole verification pass was graded against an exe whose manifest sha was wrong, and one deploy lane is recorded as poisoned as a baseline by four independent lanes.
  • Fixtures that cannot fail. Four visual bookmark fixtures were numerically identical copies of one template framing empty terrain, and a verification region rect pointed at an off-map slab instead of the lake. Both "passed" continuously while the defects they named were live. Both were deleted or re-aimed.
  • The capture harness was blind to a whole bug class because the runner silently forced all units visible by default.
  • Status docs went stale within a day, repeatedly and in the dangerous direction. That is why §0 and the gate column above are rebuilt from source at render time and never read from a document.
  • Small-resolution A/B under-reports. One lane established that 800×600 systematically hides this defect class; another that night light pools drift ~7% run-to-run, making naive full-frame numeric A/B meaningless at mc2_10 night.

sections.heading: Instruments that lied — the session's real throughline

blocks.html: This is the most reusable thing on the page. Again and again the expensive failure was not a wrong fix — it was a measurement that reported success while seeing nothing. Every item below is a real instrument that returned a passing or confident reading while blind, mis-scoped, or measuring a different quantity than the one it was named for. Several of them invalidated multiple lanes' evidence before being caught.

• Four bookmark fixtures were the same file. mc2_03/10/17/24.json were numerically identical to each other — one template copy-pasted — each advertising distinct coverage, each framing empty terrain. They passed continuously while the defects they claimed to cover were live. Deleted rather than repaired. (VERIFY-INTEGRITY-3)
  • A camera-pinning gate the smoke runner threw away. MC2_CAMERA_PARK was never in run_smoke.py's passthrough allowlist, so every pose-pinned smoke run silently measured the default camera instead of the requested pose. All prior pose-pinned evidence gathered that way is suspect. (LIGHT-CLUSTER-PERF-1.) Note the precise scope: CAPTURE-DETERMINISM-1 checked the other harness and refuted the same claim for run_visual_capture.py, which copies the environment and strips nothing — the defect was real in one runner and not the other.
  • A perf harness reporting CPU time for a GPU cost. tracy_capture_compare.py reported CPU-side DrawScreen zone duration as “frame time” for a fully async GL pipeline, so raising per-fragment work 4× moved the number by 0.2%. The real signal was sitting in the discarded column all along — frame counts differed by 12% while the reported p50s did not move. (PERF-HARNESS-TRUTH-1)
  • Nine perf logs that were zero bytes. MC2_LOG was never set and stdout went to NUL, so all nine .game.log files were empty. There was no receipt that the pose, gate or mission had ever applied — the runs were not merely wrong, they were unverifiable. Results were reported anyway. (PERF-HARNESS-TRUTH-1)
  • A determinism ratchet that globbed the wrong depth. It looked for r1/*.png, one flat level; captures nest two deep as crops/<bookmark>/<region>.png. On a real 234-PNG, three-run, visibly noisy set it found 0 files, printed SKIP and exited 0 — indistinguishable from a check that cannot fail. Once fixed it immediately caught 12 known-bad regions and 2 more that had already been blessed. (DETERMINISM-RATCHET-2)
  • deterministic: true meant only “the gate was set”. The sidecar flag is literally SmokeMode::fixedTimestepEnabled(). Frames differing by 27% of pixels carried it. docs/visual-verify.md had claimed the engine stamps the flag honestly; that claim is now corrected. (CAPTURE-DETERMINISM-1)
  • A clock probe that agreed with itself. [SMOKE_CLOCK_PROBE] is indexed by sim frame and prints scenarioTime, which is a pure function of that index — it matches tautologically and proves nothing. Captures trigger on a different counter, render frames. Fixed by recording sim_frame beside frame so the two can actually be compared. (CAPTURE-DETERMINISM-1)
  • PASS (5/5) printed directly above DEPLOY_FINGERPRINT MISMATCH. A tier1 run reports pass while smoking a foreign lane's executable. Eight separate lanes hit this trap before it was closed. The standing rule it produced: a PASS line alone is not evidence; the fingerprint line is. (SHADOW-DECISIONS-1, IBL-NIGHT-SCALE-1, PROP-BASE-LIGHT-DIR-1)
  • 620 gates strippable by harnesses, not the 101 believed. The registry-debt survey was off by roughly an order of magnitude: 620 gates are read by code but absent from the smoke passthrough allowlist (830 unregistered, 726 undocumented, 5 genuine ghosts). Every one of those is a silent gate-OFF run wearing a gate-ON label. Compounding it, check-env-registry.sh was itself found blind to ~142 readers. (DETERMINISM-RATCHET-2, overturning VERIFY-INTEGRITY-3's figure)
  • A disk that hit zero and said nothing. The A: volume reached 0 bytes free mid-capture; four runs failed at 76 s and 12 of 14 PNGs in one arm were written zero-byte. Half of LIGHT-REALISM-FLIP-1's matrix — including a required verify-by-exaggeration arm — was never run. (LIGHT-REALISM-FLIP-1)
  • Pixel A/B itself, at mc2_10 night. A noise-floor control with byte-identical environment on both arms showed captures differing by up to 24.3%, later reproduced at 27.3%. Several reported “effects” of 21-26% changed pixels were therefore indistinguishable from launch-to-launch noise. Lanes had to fall back to numeric diagnostics to get any trustworthy verdict at all. (CONE-SPILL-GRADE-1, CAPTURE-DETERMINISM-1)

The pattern worth keeping. In every case the instrument's failure mode was silence: an empty set treated as a pass, a stripped variable warned about but not refused, a flag that reported intent instead of outcome, a zero-byte file accepted as a result. The repairs that stuck all took the same shape — make the instrument prove it can see: empty-set-now-fails, ENV-DROP promoted from warning to refusal, receipt assertions on non-zero logs, and --selftest assertions that fail on synthetic violations.

sections.heading: 19. Concrete tone — ARM A vs ARM B vs ARM C (your choice)

blocks.html:
The user's ruling: "do 3, in the index.html — also ... by all concrete I mean only the actual concrete ... obviously runways, roads, other overlays etc. are their own layer and are currently handled by the shader." Two arms are built, both default OFF, and presented here to choose from. Neither is recommended by the lane — the frames are the decision.

ARM A MC2_CEMENT_CONCRETE_TONE=1 — each concrete cell keeps its own art; only its base tone is pulled onto one reference. ARM B MC2_CEMENT_CONCRETE_CANON=1 — every plain-concrete tile samples one canonical cell, so concrete cannot change colour tile to tile at all. Both act only on cells passing an explicit is-this-actually-concrete test (near-neutral chroma ≤ 0.20, band luminance within [0.72,1.32] of the family centre).

SCOPE QUESTION ANSWERED — markings do NOT live in the concrete cells. This is what blocked the previous lane, and the ruling is confirmed twice over. From source: the solid-cement map g_cementLayerIndexBySlot that ARM B repoints is built only from slots where isCement && !isAlpha; alpha cells are explicitly skipped when it is filled, and TileIsRoadArt() says it outright — a slot present in that map is "solid cement, not road". Runway and road art arrives either as an &Overlays id (its own sampler and blend, u_overlaySidecar / terrain_overlay.frag) or as a cement-alpha transition cell, which is appended past the solid range both arms operate on. From measurement: the cement atlas was dumped (new MC2_CEMENT_ATLAS_DUMP diagnostic) and inspected — on mc2_24, not one of the 110 solid cells has a single texel more than 45 luma above its band mean (largest excursion ~11). There is no painted marking art in solid concrete cells to erase. The census reports family_marked=0; a map that does pack paint into a solid cell is detected (>2% of texels >60 luma above band) and excluded from ARM B by index.

MEASURED — and it reframes the problem. Dumping the atlas showed cross-cell base tone is far more uniform than assumed: on mc2_24 the median cell sits at L=146.3 with p05–p95 = 133–148. What actually varies is inside the cells — 78 of 110 cells carry a large dark region, 36–52% of the tile at L≈60 against concrete at L≈147. That in-cell dark art, not cross-cell tone, is the dominant reason concrete reads as changing colour here. It is why ARM B (which replaces the whole cell) moves ~11–15 luma while ARM A (which only rescales base tone) moves ~1–2.

HONEST CAVEAT ON ARM A — read before grading. On mc2_24 ARM A's census line is family=110 adjusted=96 ref_rgb=149.0,146.4,138.4, which is numerically identical to the census of the gate already rejected (MC2_CEMENT_TONE_MATCH, "after is WAY worse"). On that map every solid cell passes the concrete test, so concrete-only scoping buys nothing and ARM A is that rejected lever with a narrower clamp. It differs only where a map packs genuinely non-concrete cement cells. If mc2_24 is the reference, expect to reject ARM A again — the lane will not claim otherwise.

blocks.html: ARM C — what the “dark regions” actually are

A correction to this section, from measurement. The two arms above were built on the premise that solid concrete cells carry no road or marking art — stated in this pack as “markings do NOT live in the concrete cells”, and supported by a test that found no texel more than 45 luma above its cell band. That test looked only at the bright side. The large dark region it then found in 78 of 110 mc2_24 cells was recorded as “authored material (joints, tarmac, shadowed detail)”.

Dumping the atlas and rendering it shows what it is: a baked asphalt road tileset — straights, curves, T-junctions, crossroads with crosswalk stripes, end caps and a multi-lane highway-with-guardrail piece, painted onto a concrete background. Asphalt is dark, which is precisely why the bright-side test could not see it.

blocks.html:
The reframe this forces — there is no concrete tone problem. Measured with the road texels excluded, the concrete background is already one colour on every map: mc2_24 144.7–149.5 (spread 4.7 luma, std 0.89), mc2_05 3.2, mc2_03 2.4, mc2_10 2.0. mc2_23 and mc2_01 show a ~43-luma span driven entirely by two and one cells, and those cells are wide highway pieces — not concrete.

What makes concrete “magically become a different color” inside a cell is a road: background L≈147 against asphalt L≈82, a ~65-luma hard-edged step. That is exactly the class you scoped out — “obviously runways, roads, other overlays etc. are their own layer and are currently handled by the shader.” True for the &Overlays class. Not true for this one: it is baked into the terrain texture catalog, so TileIsRoadArt() reports “solid cement, not road” and every concrete lever treats a road as concrete.
What ARM C does

ARM C MC2_CEMENT_ROAD_ART_DETECT=1 — detect the baked road art and exclude those cells from every concrete treatment (ARM A's tone pass, ARM B's remap, and the choice of canonical cell). Each cell is split against its own [P60,P95] upper mode — the concrete background — rather than the whole-cell band mean, which on a road-heavy cell is dragged down by the road and hides it. A cell with more than 5% of its texels more than 40 luma below that background is flagged as carrying road art.

ARM C on its own changes no pixels. It writes nothing to the atlas and nothing to the slot→layer map; it only changes which cells ARM A and ARM B are allowed to touch. Its purpose is to make the concrete arms obey your own scope ruling.

What ARM C prevents, measured in-engine. Without it, ARM B repoints 90–100% of the road-carrying cells at its canonical cell — and on 5 of the 6 maps that canonical cell is itself a road tile. On mc2_24 the engine logs canon_cell=10 canon_road_frac=0.312 remapped=109 kept_road=0: ARM B erases every junction, curve and end cap and stamps one straight road segment across every plain concrete tile on the map. With ARM C the same map logs canon_cell=0 canon_road_frac=0.000 remapped=31 kept_road=78 — only the genuinely plain cells are collapsed, and the road network survives intact.

blocks.html: Measurements (two-run floor published first; ⛔ = floor exceeds the effect, no claim)

How to read this. ARM B+C % px is 0.0 on every floor-valid pose on mc2_23, mc2_24 and mc2_05. That is not ARM C being weak — it means that on those views, 100% of ARM B's measured effect was road destruction. Once roads are protected there is nothing left for ARM B to do, because every concrete cell in frame carries road art.

Hard-step % (adjacent-pixel luma jump > 16 — the metric that sank MC2_PAVED_OVERLAY_CLASS at 0.6–10.8pp): ARM B alone raises it by up to +0.618pp (mc2_24 saved_192316, 3.079→3.697). ARM B + ARM C returns it to the OFF value exactly on every floor-valid pose — ARM C's own hard-step delta is 0.000pp.

Intra-cell spread is unchanged by ARM C, deliberately: the ~65-luma step from concrete (L≈147) to asphalt (L≈82) is the road, and ARM C exists to protect it. Cross-cell concrete-background span, from the engine's own census: mc2_24 bg_span=17.6, mc2_23 18.0, mc2_05 6.9. Offline, with a stricter road exclusion, mc2_24 measures 4.7 — the shipped in-engine estimate is conservative on the heaviest crossroads cells and overstates the span. Either number says the same thing: the concrete is one colour.

Honest limits. (1) ARM C does not make the airbase look different on its own — by design it is a pixel no-op. If you want a visible change here, the frames above say the candidate is OFF, not any arm. (2) This lane did not establish why the mc2_23 apron reads as patchy to you if the concrete is one colour; the remaining suspects are the tile-level lighting term and how the road tileset pieces are placed on the map (a mismatched piece leaves a stub or a broken run), neither of which is an atlas-tone question. (3) Poses marked ⛔ carry no claim — their two-run floor exceeds the effect.
